The payload is therefore not JSON-serializable and relies on pickle; if JSON serialization is used, apply_async will fail. Even when a custom encoder stringifies the datetime, from_dict does not parse it back. Serialize queued explicitly, for example as an ISO-8601 string, and deserialize it in from_dict."

findings.title: AssignmentSource.queued default is evaluated once at import
findings.body: The dataclass declares queued: datetime = timezone.now(), so the default is evaluated once when the module is imported rather than per instance. All AssignmentSource objects created via from_integration will carry the same process-start timestamp, making the field misleading and unsafe for any future freshness/TTL logic. Use field(default_factory=timezone.now).

findings.title: to_dict() produces a non-JSON-safe Celery payload
findings.body: to_dict returns asdict(self), leaving queued as a Python datetime. This dict is passed directly to Celery as task kwargs in sync_group_assignee_outbound. The payload is therefore not JSON-serializable and relies on pickle; if JSON serialization is used, apply_async will fail. Even when a custom encoder stringifies the datetime, from_dict does not parse it back. Serialize queued explicitly, for example as an ISO-8601 string, and deserialize it in from_dict.

findings.title: New Celery task kwarg is not backward compatible with old workers
findings.body: The task signature adds assignment_source_dict, but old workers have a sync_assignee_outbound function that accepts only external_issue_id, user_id, and assign. In a mixed-version deploy, new producers can enqueue tasks with the new kwarg and old workers will raise TypeError, causing assignee sync failures and retries. This needs a backward-compatible task rollout or compatibility handling.

findings.title: Tasks are still enqueued for the integration that triggered the change
findings.body: sync_group_assignee_outbound enqueues a task for every linked external issue, including issues belonging to the integration identified by assignment_source. Each of those tasks loads ExternalIssue, Organization, Integration, and installation only to exit because should_sync returns False. For frequent inbound assignment webhooks this creates avoidable Celery tasks and database/service lookups; filtering out the source integration before enqueuing would be cheaper.

findings.title: Invalid assignment source silently disables cycle protection
findings.body: When assignment_source_dict is present but AssignmentSource.from_dict cannot construct an object, parsed_assignment_source becomes None and the task proceeds as if no source were provided. That silently removes the cycle protection for malformed or version-skewed payloads. At minimum, record a log or metric for unparsable assignment_source_dict; ideally make the payload schema stable and validate required fields.

findings.title: No test that deassignment with a matching AssignmentSource is suppressed
findings.body: The added test covers suppression for GroupAssignee.objects.assign with a matching AssignmentSource, but there is no analogous test for GroupAssignee.objects.deassign with a matching AssignmentSource. Since deassignment also triggers sync_group_assignee_outbound, a regression in the deassign path could reintroduce sync cycles without being caught.
